---
kind: mdbase.type
name: reader-source
version: 1
description: A source and user-authored literature note for mdbase Reader.
schema:
  dialect: json-schema-2020-12
  value:
    $schema: https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema
    type: object
    additionalProperties: true
    required: [type, id, title, kind, saved_at]
    properties:
      type: { const: reader-source }
      id: { type: string, minLength: 1 }
      title: { type: string, minLength: 1 }
      kind: { type: string, minLength: 1 }
      authors:
        type: array
        items: { type: string }
      published:
        oneOf:
          - type: string
          - type: number
      url: { type: string }
      description: { type: string }
      language: { type: string }
      saved_at: { type: string, format: date-time }
      documents:
        type: array
        items:
          type: object
          additionalProperties: true
          required: [file]
          properties:
            file_id: { type: string }
            file: { type: string, minLength: 1 }
            role: { type: string }
            revision: { type: string, pattern: "^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$" }
            format: { type: string }
            media_type: { type: string }
            label: { type: string }
      reading:
        type: object
        additionalProperties: true
        properties:
          status: { type: string }
          progress: { type: number, minimum: 0, maximum: 1 }
      tags:
        type: array
        items:
          type: [string, number, boolean]
      relations:
        type: array
        items:
          type: object
          additionalProperties: true
          required: [relation, target]
          properties:
            relation: { type: string }
            target: { type: string }
      csl: { type: object }
collection:
  unique:
    - field: id
      scope: type
  links:
    documents[].file:
      target_type: any
      validate_exists: true
    relations[].target:
      target_type: reader-source
      validate_exists: false
implements:
  - contract: dev.mdbase.reader.source
    version: 1.0.0-beta.1
    fields:
      id: id
      title: title
      kind: kind
      authors: authors
      published: published
      url: url
      description: description
      language: language
      saved_at: saved_at
      documents: documents
      reading: reading
      tags: tags
      relations: relations
      csl: csl

kind: mdbase.contract
contract_type: record
id: mdbase.app-settings
version: 1.0.0
name: App settings
description: One record per app holding the policy that app's clients honour in this collection.
record_schema:
  dialect: json-schema-2020-12
  ref: ../../schemas/mdbase.app-settings/1.0.0.schema.json
---

# App settings

An app settings record holds values that every client of one app honours in this
collection, such as how new files are named. The values change client behaviour,
never what another record means.

## Location and identity

A collection-scope record lives at `_settings/<app>.md`, where `<app>` is the
record's `app` field. Clients read it by that path, without a query. Each
implementing type declares `collection.unique` on `app` with `scope: type`, so a
collection holds at most one collection-scope record per app.

The record's `type` field names the app's own settings type, not a shared value.
Generic tools find every settings record through this contract.

## Reserved fields

- `app`: the app id.
- `scope`: `collection`, or `user` for one person's overrides.
- `user`: a link to an `mdbase.person` record, present only when `scope` is
  `user`.
- `settings_version`: the version of the app's settings schema that last wrote
  the record.

Every other frontmatter field belongs to the app and is described by the app's
own settings contract. The body is free Markdown for people; apps never parse it.

## Client behaviour

- A missing record means every setting has its default. Clients never create the
  record on read.
- A missing or invalid field takes its default; valid fields are used as
  written. The record is not rewritten until someone saves.
- A save creates the record at its fixed path the first time, and otherwise
  patches only the fields it changes, guarded by the record's revision.
- A client that finds a `settings_version` newer than it understands treats the
  settings as read-only and uses them as written.

## Authority

This artifact is passive. A settings record grants nothing and must never hold
secrets: anyone who can read or write records can read or edit it.

---
kind: mdbase.contract
contract_type: record
id: dev.mdbase.reader.settings
version: 1.1.0
name: mdbase Reader settings
description: Collection-wide mdbase Reader settings, such as how new files are named and what highlight colours mean.
record_schema:
  dialect: json-schema-2020-12
  ref: ../../schemas/dev.mdbase.reader.settings/1.1.0.schema.json
---

# mdbase Reader settings

The collection's settings record for mdbase Reader, at
`_settings/dev.mdbase.reader.md`. It also implements `mdbase.app-settings`, whose
reserved fields (`app`, `scope`, `settings_version`) it shares.

## Name templates

`source_name_template` and `annotation_name_template` are
[Knap](https://knap.md) templates that choose the preferred file name of a new
source note or annotation. Reader always makes the result safe for every file
system, and falls back to its own names when the result is empty, unusable or
taken. A name is chosen once, when the record is created: changing a template
never renames existing files.

Source note templates may contain `/` to put notes in folders under `sources/`.
Annotations always go directly under `annotations/`.

Variables for source notes: `title`, `authors`, `author` (the first author's family
name), `year`, `type`, `publisher`, `site`, `id`, `short_id` and `date`, plus
`parent_title`, `parent_author`, `parent_year` and `parent_stem` for chapters.

Variables for annotations: `id`, `short_id`, `type`, `quote`, `words`, `page`,
`color`, `date` and `source_stem`.

Filters: `slug`, `lower`, `upper`, `capitalize`, `title`, `trim`, `truncate`,
`replace`, `split`, `join`, `first`, `last`, `slice`, `length` and `date`.

## Highlight colours

Reader has five highlight colours: `yellow`, `green`, `blue`, `pink` and `purple`.
An annotation stores only its colour.

`highlight_colors` lists the colours Reader offers when making or recolouring a
highlight, in the order it offers them. It has at least one colour and none twice;
Reader ignores colours it does not know. A colour left out is not removed: its
highlights still draw in that colour, show in filters and can be recoloured. When
the colour last used is left out, Reader makes new highlights in the first colour
listed. Without the field, Reader offers all five in the order above.

`highlight_meanings` gives a colour a short label, at most 40 characters, such as
`pink: Question`. Because highlights store only their colour, changing a meaning
relabels every highlight already in that colour. A colour without a meaning is
called by its name.

## Versions

1.1.0 adds `highlight_colors` and `highlight_meanings` to 1.0.0. Both are optional,
so every 1.0.0 record is a 1.1.0 record, and `settings_version` stays 1.

## Authority

This artifact is passive and grants nothing.

---
kind: mdbase.type
name: reader-settings
version: 2
description: mdbase Reader's collection-wide settings, one record at _settings/dev.mdbase.reader.md.
schema:
  dialect: json-schema-2020-12
  ref: ../schemas/dev.mdbase.reader.settings/1.1.0.schema.json
collection:
  unique:
    - field: app
      scope: type
implements:
  - contract: mdbase.app-settings
    version: 1.0.0

# Saved view

A record exposed through `mdbase.view` stores shared query scope and one or more
stable named views. Each named view resolves to the query model in Chapter 11.
Optional `presentation` metadata is advisory and does not alter headless query
results.

Implementing this contract is how a collection declares which of its records
are saved views. A tool that advertises `view_records` discovers and executes
views through this contract's type implementations, not through a reserved type
name, path, or frontmatter value.

This artifact is passive. Implementing it grants no authority to read, execute,
or modify any record.
